text: Every standard catalog item generates a Request and one or more Requested Items that move through the normal approval and fulfillment lifecycle. A Record Producer is a special type of catalog item, stored on sc_cat_item_producer, that breaks from that path entirely — when submitted, it creates a record directly on a target table of the administrator's choosing, often incident, with no Request or Requested Item generated at all.

Take a Report an Outage example. An end user just wants to say the building's Wi-Fi is down, and sending them through a full request-and-fulfillment flow is overkill for something that's really just an incident with a friendlier face. The requester sees a short catalog form — what's affected, where, how many people affected, a description — nothing more.

Behind the scenes, the Record Producer's target table is set to incident, and each variable is mapped to a real field on the Incident form. The moment the requester submits, ServiceNow creates an actual Incident record populated from those mappings and routes them straight to it. From the requester's point of view they used the catalog; from the system's point of view, they filed an incident directly.

This mapping is conceptually similar to how a standard catalog item's variables eventually populate a Requested Item, except a Record Producer writes directly to whatever table you've pointed it at, with no sc_req_item layer in between at all. Get the mapping wrong, and the new incident record is created with blank or incorrect fields no one notices until fulfillment.

So which do you build? Choose a standard catalog item when the request needs to be tracked through approvals and fulfillment tasks — most hardware and access requests. Choose a Record Producer when the real goal is a record on a different table altogether, where the standard Request layer would add no fulfillment value of its own.

Get this choice backwards in either direction and it costs real time: forcing an outage report through a full approval chain delays triage, and building a Record Producer for something that actually needed approvals throws that tracking away.
